Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mrpheus 0.1.4.9000 (development)

🛏️ stage_epochs(): now reproduces YASA (results change)

stage_epochs() is checked against yasa.SleepStaging (YASA 0.8.1, scipy 1.18.1) feature by feature and probability by probability. Three errors in the feature code, a missing model selection and a missing precision step are fixed; on the public night used to check this, the stage is now the same as YASA’s in every epoch.

  • Channel-specific classifiers. YASA picks one of eight classifiers from the channels given (EEG, EEG + EOG, EEG + EMG, EEG + EOG + EMG, each with or without demographics). mrpheus shipped only the EEG + EOG + EMG model and filled missing channels with NA. With EOG absent that gave 50% accuracy against manual scoring on the test night (YASA: 83%); with EMG absent it differed from YASA’s EEG + EOG model in 91 of 780 epochs. All eight are now bundled as inst/models/yasa_<channels>[_demo].txt.gz (about 3.3 MB each) and chosen automatically. New arguments age and male select the +demo classifiers; model_path now defaults to NULL (automatic) and accepts .gz files. The result carries the classifier as attr(, "classifier"). Run data-raw/fetch_yasa_models.py to create the model files; the old inst/models/yasa_staging.txt is byte-identical to yasa_eeg_eog_emg and can be deleted.
  • Single precision. YASA rounds all features to float32 before predicting; mrpheus now does too.
  • Simpson integration for an even number of points. .scipy_simpson() used a 3/8-rule variant; scipy (1.13.1 to 1.18.1 checked, see Caveats) uses Cartwright’s correction on the last interval. This changed the 0.4-1 Hz and 1-4 Hz band powers (even point counts at 0.2 Hz resolution) and the delta ratios built from them, by up to half a standard deviation, and also affects compute_band_power() and compute_temporal_bandpower() wherever a band holds an even number of frequency bins. The old tests used linear data, which every Simpson variant integrates exactly, so they could not see it.
  • Skewness and kurtosis standardised with the sample (n - 1) standard deviation; YASA uses population central moments. The normalised variants cancel the difference, the raw ones (which the classifiers also use) did not. A flat epoch now gives NaN skew and kurtosis, as in YASA.
  • Zero crossings now follow antropy.num_zerocross (np.signbit): an exact zero is no longer counted as two crossings.

Measured agreement. On Sleep-EDF SC4001E0 (6.5 h, 780 epochs), 100 Hz and 256 Hz inputs, all 16 classifier configurations give the same stage in every epoch as YASA, with probabilities equal to about 1e-16 in 99.9% of epochs. The exception is the recording’s first and last sample: the zero-phase FIR filter’s output there is zero by construction and its sign is floating-point noise (+6e-15 in MNE, -4e-14 here), so one zero-crossing count can differ by one. Because robust_scale uses whole-column quantiles this shifts every epoch’s normalised value slightly; the largest probability difference seen was 1e-3, in one epoch of 12,480. Taking only the zero-crossing features from YASA makes the probabilities exactly identical (difference 0.0). tests/testthat/test-yasa-parity.R checks all eight classifiers against a stored YASA reference. The earlier “validated” parity script compared at MAE 0.01 and skipped 15 edge epochs; that was not parity to float precision.

Caveats. YASA 0.8.1 requires scipy >= 1.15 (its PyPI metadata). Measured with YASA 0.8.1 on a synthetic 2 h recording (240 epochs) under scipy 1.13.1, 1.14.1, 1.15.0, 1.16.3, 1.17.1 and 1.18.1 (numpy 2.5, pandas 2.3.3; 1.13.1 and 1.14.1 are below YASA’s own requirement and were run anyway): features and class probabilities are identical on 1.13.1 to 1.17.1; 1.18.1 differs in one zero crossing count in the first epoch (EMG channel: 577 against 578; the EOG channel also changes), which moves one probability by up to 1.1e-3 and no stage; band power agrees to 1e-13 and the events of sw_detect and spindles_detect to 6e-14. Versions before 1.13 were not tested (YASA 0.8.1 needs numpy >= 2.2.2, which scipy 1.12 and older do not support), so nothing is claimed for them. Preprocessing with preprocess_psg() before staging is not what YASA does and changes the result (84 of 780 epochs on the test night, mostly through the EOG band-pass); stage from unpreprocessed signals to reproduce YASA.

📊 compute_band_power(): now follows yasa.bandpower() (results change)

The defaults did not match YASA’s, although the help page said they did. On Sleep-EDF SC4001E0 (780 epochs, two channels, at 100 and 256 Hz; YASA 0.8.1) the old defaults differed from yasa.bandpower() by a median of 6 to 12% per band and epoch in absolute power (and in relative power), with a few epochs far larger. The defaults are now YASA’s, and the result agrees with yasa.bandpower() to about 1e-14 relative in absolute power and about 1e-12 in relative power (maximum over all epochs, channels and both sampling rates; also checked against yasa.bandpower() itself on ten epochs).

  • Segment averaging: the bias-corrected median of scipy (average = "median"), not the mean. This is the largest single difference, about 10% of band power at the median and more than 200% at the 99th percentile of epochs.
  • Window: Hamming, not Hann (about 2%), and the periodic form that scipy.signal.welch uses. mrpheus built the symmetric form, which alone gave up to 0.8% in absolute band power with every other setting matched. New argument window ("hamming" or "hann").
  • nfft and noverlap default to NULL: the window length (YASA’s, scipy’s) and half a window. The old defaults of 1024 and 200 samples differed from that by about 3% (nfft, at 100 Hz) and 7% (overlap, at 256 Hz); 200 samples is half a window only at 100 Hz.
  • Gamma is 30-40 Hz (YASA’s default bands), not 30-45 Hz.
  • Relative power is a band’s Simpson integral divided by the PSD integral between the lowest and highest band edge, as in YASA, and no longer divided by the sum of the band powers. The two are equal when the bands tile that range and their edges fall on FFT bins (the new defaults), but differed by a median of 0.7% and up to 5.7% at 100 Hz with nfft = 1024. total_power is now that integral (YASA’s TotalAbsPow), not the sum of the band powers.
  • relative now defaults to TRUE, as YASA’s does (it was FALSE); use relative = FALSE for absolute power.
  • The old estimate can be requested with window = "hann", average = "mean", noverlap = 200L, nfft = 1024L and bands with gamma c(30, 45), except that the window is now the periodic form.

compute_temporal_bandpower() is unchanged (its output is identical to before): it has no YASA counterpart, it keeps its own settings (symmetric Hann window, mean, gamma 30-45 Hz) and agrees with an independent scipy implementation of the same method to about 1e-13. Its help page no longer says that its default bands match compute_band_power().

tests/testthat/test-yasa-bandpower-parity.R compares compute_band_power() with a stored yasa.bandpower() reference (data-raw/generate_yasa_bandpower_parity_fixture.py); each of the old settings above makes it fail, apart from the relative-power definition, which test-compute_band_power.R checks with bands that leave a gap.

The “Parity with YASA” section of the spectral-analysis vignette and the README wording are rewritten. They described the old settings as validated, and put the ~0.75% relative-power gap down to floating-point accumulation; it was the relative-power definition. The vignette now reports the measured agreement on SC4001E0 (2,650 epochs): at most 8e-15 relative in absolute power and 1e-12 in relative power. The old validation scripts data-raw/validate_band_power_parity.R and data-raw/generate_bandpower_reference.py, which used the old settings, and their reference and report files (yasa_reference_bandpower.csv, parity_report_bandpower.csv, parity_bandpower.png) are removed.

🌊 compute_slow_oscillations(): now reproduces yasa.sw_detect() (results change)

The detector is a port of yasa.sw_detect() (YASA 0.8.1). On the Sleep-EDF night SC4001E0 (Fpz-Cz; 8.8 h at 100 Hz, and a 6.5 h version at 256 Hz), with a stage mask that cuts through events, it finds the same events as YASA: the same numbers (2,236 and 1,000), event times identical to the sample, and amplitudes within about 1e-12 uV. The previous version, which paired zero crossings, found about 20% fewer events than YASA on one night (4.7 against 5.9 per NREM minute, from a Python mirror of it).

  • Filter. An FIR band-pass equivalent to mne.filter.filter_data() (Hamming window, zero phase, 0.3-1.5 Hz with 0.2 Hz transition bands) is applied to the whole continuous signal, not epoch by epoch, instead of a Butterworth cascade. The design equals mne.filter.create_filter to about 1e-16 (checked at 100, 125, 128, 200, 250, 256, 500 and 512 Hz) and the filtered signal equals filter_data to about 5e-13 uV. This also removes the old failure at 256 Hz (“system is computationally singular”) and the sample-rate limit of the cascade.
  • Detection. Peaks of the filtered signal are found as scipy.signal.find_peaks does (negative peaks with a trough of 40-200 uV, positive peaks of 10-150 uV) and kept if they lie in the accepted epochs. Each negative peak is paired with the closest following positive peak, the peak-to-peak amplitude must be 75-350 uV, and the durations of the two phases, taken from the zero crossings around the peaks, must be 0.3-1.5 s and 0.1-1.0 s. Events that share their start, and then their end, with another event are dropped, as in YASA (so two negative peaks paired with the same positive peak are both lost). The zero-crossing pairing of the old version, and its polarity bug (an epoch whose filtered signal started negative returned no events), are gone; detect_so_candidates_cpp() and its tests are removed.
  • stages are the epochs in which the peaks must lie. As in YASA, an event can start or end outside them.
  • Output. epoch is the epoch of the negative peak, and start_s and end_s, relative to it, can lie outside 0-30 s for an event that crosses an epoch boundary. New columns: neg_peak_s, mid_crossing_s, pos_peak_s (seconds from the start of the first epoch) and slope_uv_s.
  • Arguments. transition_hz is now the width of both transition bands of the FIR filter (default 0.2, as YASA); zero is rejected, so the old behaviour can no longer be requested through it. The other defaults are YASA’s, as before.
  • A channel whose trimmed standard deviation (central 90% of samples) is outside 0.1-1000 uV is skipped with a warning, as in YASA.
  • Not implemented: YASA’s slow oscillation - spindle coupling and remove_outliers.
  • Tests. tests/testthat/test-yasa-slow-oscillation-parity.R compares the result with stored yasa.sw_detect() output on a synthetic EEG at 100 and 256 Hz, the filter taps with mne.filter.create_filter, and the detection with YASA’s own code on a crafted signal that reaches its edge cases (plateaus, double-humped waves, limits exactly on the boundary, exact zeros) (data-raw/generate_yasa_slow_oscillation_parity_fixture.py). Putting each deviation back one at a time, 11 of 13 make the tests fail; the other two change nothing (removing only the shared-end check, and the wrap-around of the previous zero crossing before the first one).

💤 compute_spindles(): now reproduces yasa.spindles_detect() (results change)

The detector is a port of yasa.spindles_detect() (YASA 0.8.1). On the Sleep-EDF night SC4001E0 (Fpz-Cz; 8.8 h at 100 Hz, and a 6.5 h version at 256 Hz), with a stage mask that cuts through events, it finds the same spindles as YASA: the same numbers (73 and 78), start and end times identical to the sample, and every property within about 1e-11. The previous version (a 11-16 Hz Butterworth band-pass and an RMS threshold of 1.5 standard deviations, both per epoch, and a Welch peak frequency) was a different method and had not been compared with YASA.

  • Algorithm. Two MNE-equivalent FIR filters are applied to the whole continuous signal: a broadband (1-30 Hz) and a sigma (12-15 Hz, 1.5 Hz transition bands). Three criteria are evaluated at every sample: the relative sigma power of a short-time Fourier transform (2 s windows every 0.2 s), the moving correlation between the sigma and the broadband signal (0.3 s windows) and the moving RMS of the sigma signal (threshold: mean plus 1.5 trimmed standard deviations within the accepted epochs, at most 10 uV). The number of criteria met is smoothed over 0.1 s, events where all are met are kept, events closer than 500 ms are merged, and durations of 0.5-2 s are accepted.
  • Arguments. freq_spindle now defaults to c(12, 15) (was c(11, 16)). New: freq_broad, duration_s (replaces min_duration_s and max_duration_s; the maximum is 2 s, was 3 s), min_distance_ms, thresh_rel_pow, thresh_corr and thresh_rms (replaces threshold_sd; NULL switches a criterion off). rms_window_s is removed: the window is fixed at 0.3 s, as in YASA.
  • Output. epoch is the epoch of the first sample and start_s / end_s are relative to it (end_s can exceed 30 s). peak_freq_hz is now the median instantaneous frequency (was the Welch peak) and rms_uv the RMS of the detrended broadband signal (was the mean RMS envelope). New columns: peak_s, amplitude_uv, amp_filtered_uv, abs_power, rel_power, oscillations, symmetry.
  • A channel whose trimmed standard deviation (central 90% of samples) is outside 0.1-1000 uV is skipped with a warning, as in YASA.
  • Not implemented: YASA’s multi_only, remove_outliers and spindle - slow oscillation coupling. roll_rms_cpp() and its tests are removed.
  • FIR filter length. .mne_fir_bandpass_design() rounds the filter length up to whole samples, as mne.filter does; it had rounded to nearest, which gives the same length except at rates where the length is not a whole number (for example 125 Hz, 2063 against 2062 taps for the slow oscillation filter). Checked against mne.filter.create_filter for the slow oscillation, spindle broadband and sigma filters at 100, 125, 128, 200, 250, 256, 500 and 512 Hz.
  • Tests. tests/testthat/test-yasa-spindle-parity.R compares the result with stored yasa.spindles_detect() output on a synthetic EEG with spindles at 100 and 256 Hz, and at 100 Hz on two variants (strong sigma activity in an excluded epoch; the signal times 4), plus YASA’s intermediate features (STFT relative power, moving correlation and RMS) (data-raw/generate_yasa_spindle_parity_fixture.py); test-compute_spindles.R tests the helpers against scipy and YASA values. Putting each of 19 deviations back one at a time makes the tests fail in every case; the cap of 10 uV on the RMS threshold is caught only by its direct unit test.

🔧 Resampler and spectrogram fixes

  • .mne_fft_resample() now downsamples. Staging resamples every channel to 100 Hz, so 256 Hz input (a common PSG rate) stopped with only 0's may be mixed with negative subscripts: the function only implemented the upsampling path, and the Sleep-EDF data used so far is already at 100 Hz. For a shorter output it now truncates the spectrum as MNE’s _fft_resample does (Nyquist bin doubled for an even new length, bins scaled by new_len / orig_len). A Python mirror of the new logic differs from mne.filter.resample (MNE 1.13.2) by about 5e-14 on four lengths (7,680 to 460,800 samples). The upsampling code is unchanged. Tests: tests/testthat/test-mne-fft-resample.R.
  • compute_spectrogram() overlap. The function passed noverlap to gsignal::pwelch(), which has no such argument (it takes overlap, a fraction), so the call stopped with “unused argument”. It now passes its own overlap argument (default 0.5) straight through. The function had no tests; tests/testthat/test-compute_spectrogram.R adds a synthetic 10 Hz check (it runs, returns one row per epoch, and peaks within 0.5 Hz of 10 Hz).

🚀 Performance fixes in detect_qrs()

detect_qrs() was hanging indefinitely on real recordings (unbounded on a 468,700-sample / ~15.7 min recording at ~500 Hz). Two separate O(n²) bottlenecks were found and fixed:

  • Peak selection (.find_peaks_min_dist()): was checking every candidate peak against every other accepted peak on each iteration — fine on toy data, unusable once candidate counts reach the hundreds of thousands. Replaced with a binary search (findInterval()) against a pre-allocated, sorted buffer of accepted peak locations. Note this is O(n_candidates log k
    • k²) where k is the final peak count (bounded by physiological heart rate, not by recording length), rather than a universal O(n log n) — fine here, but worth remembering if this helper is ever reused somewhere the output peak count could scale with input size.
  • Moving-average integration (Stage 4): used stats::convolve() for a plain boxcar filter. R’s FFT-based convolution can degrade badly depending on how the padded length factors for stats::nextn(), and this was the actual bottleneck once the peak-selection fix was in place. Replaced with a cumulative-sum boxcar implementation, mathematically equivalent to the FFT-based full convolution (verified numerically identical, differences on the order of 1e-15) and unconditionally O(n).

Combined effect: detect_qrs() on the 468,700-sample recording above now completes in 0.97 seconds (1855 R-peaks detected, mean HR 118 bpm).

✨ New function: compute_hrv_freq()

  • compute_hrv_freq() — frequency-domain HRV (HF power) locked to each infant’s own respiratory rate, rather than the fixed adult-derived HF band (0.15–0.4 Hz) that doesn’t apply to neonatal breathing rates (~40–70 breaths/min at rest). Detects the dominant respiratory frequency directly from the physlog’s resp channel, resamples the RR-interval series via cubic spline, and integrates Welch PSD power in a band centered on that detected frequency. Verified against synthetic data: exact frequency recovery and correct amplitude-scaling of integrated power.
  • Fills the gap left by compute_hrv_sleep(), which remains a stub expecting staged PSG input (wrong shape for physlog data) with its RR-to-HRV step never wired in — compute_hrv_freq() is a separate, physlog-shaped path rather than a completion of that stub.

🧪 Tests

  • test-find-peaks-min-dist.R: .find_peaks_min_dist() against a brute-force reference on random and periodic synthetic signals, the minimum-distance constraint, tallest-peak-wins tie-breaking (including the all-tied flat-signal edge case), and a timing regression guard on a large, realistically-smoothed candidate set.
  • test-boxcar-integration.R: the cumulative-sum boxcar formula against stats::convolve(type = "open") across several window sizes and signal lengths, plus an end-to-end detect_qrs() timing smoke test on a synthetic two-minute ECG-like signal.
  • test-compute_hrv_freq.R: synthetic QRS/respiration generators injecting a known respiratory frequency via RSA-modulated RR intervals — frequency recovery at two different frequencies, HF power scaling with RSA amplitude, band-bounds correctness, the too-few-beats NA path, and implausible-RR-interval filtering.

All fixtures are fully synthetic — no participant-derived data.

mrpheus 0.1.4 (2026-07)

🚀 Rcpp hot-path optimisation (staging pipeline + event detection)

Complete C++ hot-path port across the staging and event detection pipelines, replacing the remaining R-level bottlenecks. zoo removed from Imports.

Staging pipeline — per-epoch functions (src/staging_features.cpp):

  • nzc_cpp: zero-crossing count — single O(N) pass replacing sum(diff(sign(x)) != 0)
  • petrosian_fd_cpp: local extrema count + log formula — replaces diff + logical sum
  • hjorth_cpp: mobility and complexity — single O(N) pass accumulating all three variances (x, diff(x), diff(diff(x))) without materialising intermediate vectors
  • stat_features_cpp: std, IQR (type-7 quantile), skewness, excess kurtosis — replaces sd(), IQR() (which sorts), and two mean() calls per epoch
  • rowmedian_cpp: row-wise median of the Welch periodogram matrix — eliminates ~750 000 R median() dispatch calls per recording (251 freq bins x ~3 000 epochs)
  • roll_right_mean_cpp: right-aligned partial rolling mean (k=4), replacing zoo::rollapply for the _p2min_norm normalisation step (49 calls/recording)
  • robust_scale_cpp: (x - median) / (q95 - q5) with type-7 quantile and NA-awareness, replacing median() + quantile() for 49 normalisation calls

Event detection (src/event_detection.cpp, new file):

  • roll_rms_cpp: centered rolling RMS replacing zoo::rollapply in compute_spindles() — processes the full concatenated epoch signal per channel
  • detect_so_candidates_cpp: zero-crossing scan + duration/amplitude filtering for slow oscillation detection, replacing the R which() + lapply loop in compute_slow_oscillations()

🔧 Other changes

  • Fixed a latent bug where the pure-R vapply definition of .roll_triang_mean in the normalisation section was shadowing roll_triang_mean_cpp on every load_all(). Now a single Rcpp-backed definition exists.
  • Removed zoo from Imports — no remaining zoo:: calls anywhere in the package.

🧪 Tests

All 371 tests pass. 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes.

mrpheus 0.1.3 (2026-07)

🩺 PSG preprocessing pipeline

Full preprocessing pipeline from EDF to analysis-ready epochs, matching the companion Python/MNE notebook workflow.

  • preprocess_psg() — continuous-signal preprocessing pipeline: channel renaming, DC removal, powerline notch filter (auto-detected 50/60 Hz + harmonics), and channel-type-specific bandpass filtering (EEG/EOG/EMG/ECG). Operates on the full continuous signal before re-epoching to avoid filter discontinuities at epoch boundaries.
  • remove_dc(), detect_powerline(), notch_filter(), bandpass_filter() — exported signal-level functions; each operates on a plain numeric vector independently of the PSG pipeline.
